title: Emails with or about LexisNexis (Steele Sheriff)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting emails between your agency and LexisNexis Risk Solutions, and emails concerning LexisNexis Risk Solutions.

1) Domains: all emails between your agency and "@lexisnexis.com", "@lexisnexisrisk.com", or "@lnssi.com". Timeframe: June 15, 2026 through the date this request is completed.

2) Keywords: all emails containing "LexisNexis", "AVCC", "Accurint Virtual Crime Center", or "Lexis Nexis" in the subject or body. Timeframe: June 15, 2026 through the date this request is completed. We recommend searching "Accurint Virtual Crime Center" as a quoted phrase rather than as separate words, so the results do not include every email containing "crime" or "center."

3) Include: emails, attachments, inline and embedded images, links, and the subject and to/from/cc lines. Please provide the original emails in full.

4) Exclude: Duplicates and mass-mailings may be de-duplicated so that only a single representative example is produced. If your agency receives automated, repeating status or upload-confirmation messages, please include a sample of three rather than the full set. Some agencies receive an automated message every time a data upload to LexisNexis completes. At some departments that runs past 1,400 messages a month. We want to establish the frequency and see an example, not receive thousands of identical emails. Automated password reset and account notification emails may be excluded.

5) Format: if possible, please provide the original electronic files (.eml, .msg, .mbox, .pst, or a similar native format) so the integrity of the original messages is preserved. 

6) If any emails are withheld in whole or in part, please include a list of what was withheld and cite the specific exemption relied on for each.

7) If you coordinate or discuss the response to this request with LexisNexis in any way, please include the email, text message, meeting invite, or other media showing the conversation you had with LexisNexis relating to this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I would like to receive records of the investigative case file (Case No. MAG-98-2042-M-RLH.) and prosecution files for Larry Wayne Harris (born July 3, 1951; died January 30, 2025). Larry Wayne Harris was arrested on February 18, 1998 in Henderson, Nevada after Ronald G. Rockwell informed the FBI on February 17, 1998 that Larry Wayne Harris and William Job Leavitt Jr. claimed they had weapons-grade anthrax. Harris and Leavitt were attempting to purchase an alleged invention from Ronald G. Rockwell that purportedly could kill specific microbes using frequency. Given the location and circumstance, the Las Vegas Field Office handled the case (special agents John Hawken and Bobby Siller). Leavitt allegedly reiterated the claim over a tapped telephone line. Leavitt, Harris, and a third man were observed leaving the Gold Coast Hotel & Casino the afternoon of February 18, 1998. Leavitt and Harris drove to Daniel Royal's office where they were planning on testing Rockwell's "invention" on their microbes, located in the trunk of a white/beige Mercedes in Leavitt's possession, a gift from Gary Gerwin (aka Gary Gerwien aka Gary Griffen). The Mercedes was sealed in plastic and sent to a lab. The anthrax sample from the trunk of the Mercedes was tested to determine virulence. The sample was determined to be vaccine-grade anthrax within a few days. Leavitt was released.  Larry Wayne Harris had previously been arrested in 1995 after purchasing plague bacteria samples from ATCC under false pretenses. His conviction for wire fraud in 1995 led to a sentence of 18 months probation and he was forbidden from cultivating microbes outside a regulated lab setting. Harris received an additional six months probation for his possession of anthrax, despite violating his probation. I have included a copy of Larry Wayne Harris' obituary indicating he is deceased.
